items.question: What supreme attainment makes one dear to the yoginis?
premises: Enjoyment and liberation together constitute a great accomplishment
Such accomplishment belongs to the yoginis
One possessing it becomes dear to them
items.inference: Attaining the great accomplishment of both enjoyment and liberation makes one dear to the yoginis.
items.plain_english: One may become dear to the yoginis through the great accomplishment of both enjoyment and liberation.

items.question: Which chapter emerges in the context of the moon island?
premises: A context is described as emerged in the moon island
A chapter is identified by ordinal number
The ninth chapter is named in that context
items.inference: The ninth chapter emerges in the context of the moon island.
uncertainties: The exact referent of candra-dvīpa is not specified in this verse.
items.plain_english: The ninth chapter has emerged in the moon island.

items.question: How should the practitioner visualize the self surrounded by fire?
premises: The self is described as surrounded by fire
The self is standing on one foot
This forms a specific visualized posture
items.inference: The practitioner should visualize the self surrounded by fire and standing on one foot.
items.plain_english: Visualize the self surrounded by fire, standing on one foot.

items.question: What request is made to the god regarding the determination of knowledge?
premises: The speaker addresses the god
The determination of knowledge is the subject
The speaker asks for it to be made manifest today
items.inference: The speaker requests the god to make the determination of knowledge manifest now.
items.plain_english: O God, make the determination of knowledge manifest to me today.

items.question: What division is sought to be known fully and without end?
premises: A division of eight octads is named
There is a desire to know it fully
The knowing is sought endlessly
items.inference: The division of the eight octads is sought to be known fully and endlessly.
uncertainties: The referent of the eight octads is not specified in this verse.
items.plain_english: I seek to know fully and endlessly the division of the eight octads.

items.question: How is accomplishment attained quickly in the secret place and wheel?
premises: A secret place is identified with a wheel
Accomplishment occurs there
The accomplishment happens quickly
items.inference: In the secret place, as in the wheel, accomplishment is attained quickly.
items.plain_english: O Bhairava, in the secret place, as in the wheel, accomplishment comes quickly.

items.question: Why does Bhairava approve the great goddess's difficult question?
premises: Bhairava expresses strong approval
He addresses the great goddess
He states he was asked about something hard for gods to obtain
items.inference: Bhairava approves because the goddess has asked about a matter difficult even for the gods.
items.plain_english: Well said, well said, O great goddess! I have been asked about something hard for even the gods to obtain.

items.question: Which bodily locations are assigned to the syllables kṣa and laṃ?
premises: The syllable kṣa is associated with the state of brahmarandhra
The syllable laṃ is associated with the forehead
These are specific placements of syllables
items.inference: The syllable kṣa corresponds to the brahmarandhra and the syllable laṃ to the forehead.
uncertainties: lalāṭayoḥ is dual in form; translated as location in the forehead region.
items.plain_english: The syllable kṣa is in the brahmarandhra, and the syllable laṃ is in the forehead.

items.question: Which bodily locations are assigned to the syllables ṣa and śa?
premises: The syllable ṣa is placed in the throat region
The syllable śa is placed in the heart
These placements are stated in sequence
items.inference: The syllable ṣa corresponds to the throat region and the syllable śa to the heart.
items.plain_english: The syllable ṣa is in the throat region, and the syllable śa is then in the heart.

items.question: What instruction follows the declaration of the place-wheels?
premises: The place-wheels have been declared
Their meditation remains to be taught
The beloved is asked to listen
items.inference: After declaring the place-wheels, the teaching turns to their meditation.
items.plain_english: The place-wheels have been declared; now hear their meditation, O beloved.

items.question: How is the divine lotus of the first octad described?
premises: A divine lotus is the object of description
It has eight spokes or petals
It is adorned by the first octad
items.inference: The divine lotus is eight-spoked and adorned by the first octad.
items.plain_english: Visualize the divine eight-spoked lotus adorned by the first octad.

items.question: What conduct should a practitioner with equanimous mind abandon through practice?
premises: Practice leads to an equanimous mind
Village customs are identified as something to renounce
The practitioner is instructed to abandon them
items.inference: Through practice, one with an equanimous mind should abandon village customs.
uncertainties: dharmañ is written with final ñ; taken as accusative plural of dharma in sense of customs.
items.plain_english: Through practice, with an equanimous mind, one should abandon the customs of the village.

items.question: What powers arise from practice in this context, O beloved?
premises: Knowledge of distant hearing is named
Paralysis of bonds is named
These are presented as attainments
items.inference: The attainments include knowledge of distant hearing and the paralysis of bonds.
uncertainties: pāśa-stobham may mean arresting or immobilizing bonds; exact nuance uncertain.
items.plain_english: O beloved, one gains knowledge of distant hearing and likewise the power to paralyze bonds.

items.question: What further attainments are summarized briefly for the goddess?
premises: Immortality is named as an attainment
Transformation is named as an attainment
These are stated in brief
items.inference: In brief, the attainments include immortality and transformation.
items.plain_english: Likewise, O goddess, in brief, there are immortality and transformation.

items.question: How is the second eight-petaled wheel characterized in meditation?
premises: A second wheel is identified
It has eight petals
It is well illuminated by meditation on fire
items.inference: The second eight-petaled wheel is well illuminated through meditation on fire.
items.plain_english: The second is the eight-petaled wheel, well illuminated by meditation on fire.

items.question: What ability arises for one whose mind is absorbed in one-pointed meditation?
premises: The mind becomes absorbed in one-pointed meditation
Such a person acts with creative power
Forms can be made in many ways
items.inference: One whose mind is absorbed in one-pointed meditation can create forms in many ways.
items.plain_english: One whose mind is absorbed in one-pointed meditation can assume forms in many ways.

items.question: What destructive power does an angered adept possess over the triple world?
premises: The adept is described as angry
The entire triple world is the object
The world includes moving and unmoving beings
items.inference: When angry, the adept can destroy the entire triple world with all its moving and unmoving beings.
items.plain_english: When angry, he can destroy the entire triple world, with all that moves and does not move.

items.question: What liberating function is attributed to the third great wheel?
premises: A third great wheel is identified
Nine principles are named in relation to it
The wheel is described as a liberator
items.inference: The third great wheel is the liberator from the nine principles.
uncertainties: The specific set of nine tattvas is not identified in this verse.
items.plain_english: The third is the great wheel, the liberator from the nine principles.

items.question: What bodily and perceptual attainments are associated with this wheel?
premises: Destruction of wrinkles and grey hair is named
Seeing from very far away is named
These are presented as attainments
items.inference: The attainments include removal of wrinkles and grey hair and the ability to see from very far away.
items.plain_english: It brings the destruction of wrinkles and grey hair, and likewise the ability to see from very far away.

items.question: What practice should be performed in solitude with full intent on meditation?
premises: The practitioner is in solitude
The practitioner is intent on meditation
Creating forms in many ways is commanded
items.inference: In solitude, intent on meditation, one should create forms in many ways.
uncertainties: dhyānañ is written with final ñ; taken as accusative singular.
items.plain_english: In solitude, intent on meditation, create forms in many ways.

items.question: What result comes from being devoted to constant practice?
premises: The practitioner is devoted to constant practice
The practice produces a result
That result is immortality
items.inference: One devoted to constant practice attains immortality.
items.plain_english: Indeed, one who is devoted to constant practice attains immortality.

items.question: How does abstaining from food by day affect age and death?
premises: Non-eating by day is practiced
Age and death are the conditions faced
The practitioner will go beyond them
items.inference: By abstaining from food during the day, one will overcome age and death.
uncertainties: The compound vayo-mṛtyuṃ and the use of gamiṣyate suggest overcoming; exact idiom is somewhat compressed.
items.plain_english: By abstaining from food during the day, one will overcome age and death.

items.question: What bodily form results from constant yogic practice over sixteen years?
premises: Constant practice is joined with yoga
The duration is sixteen years
A specific form results
items.inference: Through constant yogic practice, one attains the form of a sixteen-year-old.
uncertainties: dvi-aṣṭa-varṣa-ākṛtiḥ is interpreted as the appearance of sixteen years.
items.plain_english: Through constant yogic practice, one attains the form of a sixteen-year-old.

items.question: What power arises from always contemplating a smoke-colored form?
premises: A smoke-colored form is contemplated always
The triple world is the object affected
The practitioner can cause it to shake
items.inference: By always contemplating a smoke-colored form, one can shake the triple world.
items.plain_english: O beloved, by always contemplating a smoke-colored form, one can shake the triple world.
